key_insight: A low-cost decision-only model matched or exceeded two frontier judges’ agreement with experts on average in a matched subset, but still missed many clinical omissions.
clinical_relevance: Decision-only judging could make large-scale medical AI quality monitoring more affordable, with locally validated thresholds and expert oversight.
method: Pre-registered evaluation of TypeSafe Jev 1.13 across five clinical benchmarks covering six judging tasks.
Compared agreement with expert labels against other AI judges and expert-to-expert agreement.
Assessed cost, runtime, planted-error detection and uncertainty-guided auditing.
evidence_signal: Across 25,091 units and 213,913 model calls, Jev averaged 64.7% agreement with experts; on 3,614 matched units, agreement was 66.1% versus 65.0% for Opus and 60.7% for Sol, with non-inferiority on four of six tasks.
watch_item: Agreement does not establish clinical safety: at the same false-alarm rate, Jev missed 55.6% of planted omissions, supporting continued expert review.
paper_title: A decision-only model as a low-cost judge of medical AI answers
